description: Embedded systems developer and innovator passionate about advanced technology and space solutions. Working on an independent project under the 'Nexus One' team, with a clear vision to become a founder and technology leader of a major tech enterprise in the future
summary: AriaAdapt is an advanced web-based agricultural decision-support tool developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It integrates live NASA POWER satellite telemetry (community=AG) with local user-provided sensor readings—such as soil moisture and air temperature—to bridge the gap between regional satellite data and localized field conditions. Designed specifically for farmers and smallholders facing climate volatility, the application calculates precise crop compatibility indexes, issues real-time frost and heat warnings, and provides actionable irrigation recommendations. By combining robust space data with ground-level validation in a lightweight, responsive single-file interface, AriaAdapt empowers modern farmers to optimize water consumption, safeguard crop yields, and make data-driven agricultural decisions instantly
details:
Our project is called AriaAdapt. It is a simple web tool to help farmers and people in agriculture make better decisions using NASA weather and earth data.

We made this tool because climate change makes farming very hard. Farmers need easy information about weather, soil, and water. Our app takes NASA POWER data and shows it in a very simple way so anyone can use it.

We used HTML, Tailwind CSS, and JavaScript to build a clean and fast single-page app. We also added interactive charts using Chart.js so users can see temperature and rain changes easily.

Our goal is to help local farmers save water and grow better crops using real space data.
